e-380.knowledge_point: Integrating an Exponential Function With a General Base
e-380.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constant $-6.$ Then, we integrate the exponential function, and get

$$
\eqalign{
\int (-6)7^x  \, \textrm d x   
&= -6\int 7^x\,\textrm{d}x\
&=-6 \cdot \dfrac{7^x}{\ln 7} + C.
}
$$

e-381.knowledge_point: Integrating a Sum of Exponential Functions
e-381.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\eqalign{
\displaystyle \int 5 \cdot 9^x +3 e^x  \, \textrm d x &= \displaystyle 5\int 9^x \, \textrm{d}x+ 3 \displaystyle \int e^x \, \textrm{d}x\
&= 5\cdot \dfrac{9^x}{\ln 9} + 3 e^x +C.
}
$$

decision.explanation: Use ∫a^x dx=a^x/ln(a)+C. With a=5, the integral is 5^x/ln(5)+C, option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{5}^{x}}{ln⁡5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Factor out 3 and use ∫2^x dx=2^x/ln(2)+C, giving 3·2^x/ln(2)+C.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constant $3.$ Then, we integrate the exponential function and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3\cdot {2}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =3\int {2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{2}^{x}}{ln⁡2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate ∫(18)xdx.

a
 −ln⁡x8x+C
b
 (18)xln⁡8+C
c
 ln⁡xln⁡8+C
d
−(18)xln⁡8+C
e
 8xln⁡8+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Use ∫a^x dx=a^x/ln(a)+C. Since ln(1/8)=−ln(8), the integral is −(1/8)^x/ln(8)+C.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Using the laws of logarithms, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}ln⁡(\frac{1}{8}) & =ln⁡1-ln⁡8 \\  & =0-ln⁡8 \\  & =-ln⁡8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify our final answer as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C=-\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Calculate ∫(18)xdx.

a
 −ln⁡x8x+C
b
 (18)xln⁡8+C
c
 ln⁡xln⁡8+C
d
−(18)xln⁡8+C
e
 8xln⁡8+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

∫(18)xdx=(18)xln⁡(18)+C

Using the laws of logarithms, we have that

ln⁡(18)=ln⁡1−ln⁡8=0−ln⁡8=−ln⁡8.

So, we can simplify our final answer as follows:

(18)xln⁡(18)+C=−(18)xln⁡8+C

content.knowledge_point: Integrating an Exponential Function With a General Base
content.worked_solution:
To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Using the laws of logarithms, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}ln⁡(\frac{1}{8}) & =ln⁡1-ln⁡8 \\  & =0-ln⁡8 \\  & =-ln⁡8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify our final answer as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡(\frac{1}{8})}+C=-\frac{{(\frac{1}{8})}^{x}}{ln⁡8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int (5{e}^{x}+{2}^{x})\,\text{d}x & =5\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{e}^{x}+\frac{{2}^{x}}{ln⁡2}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

∫(5ex+2x)dx=

a
5ex+2xln⁡2+C
b
5ex+xln⁡2+C
c
2ex+5xln⁡2+C
d
ex5+2xln⁡2+C
e
5ex+2xln⁡2+C
Submit

EXPLANATION

Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

∫(5ex+2x)dx=5∫exdx+∫2xdx=5ex+2xln⁡2+C.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms 5e^x+2^x/ln(2)+C. Differentiating gives 5e^x+2^x, so option a is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Sum of Exponential Functions
content.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int (5{e}^{x}+{2}^{x})\,\text{d}x & =5\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{e}^{x}+\frac{{2}^{x}}{ln⁡2}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

∫(−2ex+4x+1x)dx=

a
e−2x+4xln⁡|x|+4ln⁡|x|+C
b
ex2+xln⁡4+3ln⁡|x|+C
c
−ex+44xln⁡2+2ln⁡|x|+C
d
−2ex+2xln⁡4+3ln⁡|x|+C
e
−2ex+4xln⁡4+ln⁡|x|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrate each term: −2e^x gives −2e^x, 4^x gives 4^x/ln(4), and 1/x gives ln|x|. Adding C yields option e.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (-2{e}^{x}+{4}^{x}+\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x & =-2\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {4}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{e}^{x}+\frac{{4}^{x}}{ln⁡4}+ln⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Sum of Exponential Functions
content.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (-2{e}^{x}+{4}^{x}+\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x & =-2\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {4}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2{e}^{x}+\frac{{4}^{x}}{ln⁡4}+ln⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 13
?

∫(2ex−3x+x2)dx=

a
2ex−3xln⁡3+x33+C
b
2xln⁡2+x22−3ex+C
c
3xln⁡3+x2+ex+C
d
2e3x−32xln⁡x+x22+C
e
ex+3xln⁡2+x23+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrate term by term: 2e^x gives 2e^x, −3^x gives −3^x/ln(3), and x² gives x³/3. Adding C yields option a.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{e}^{x}-{3}^{x}+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =2\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x-\int {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{e}^{x}-\frac{{3}^{x}}{ln⁡3}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

a
2xln⁡|x|−e2x+x+C
b
5xln⁡5−2ex+2x+C
c
53xln⁡x+2e2x+x2+C
d
e3xln⁡5+2ex+x+C
e
2e5xln⁡5−ex+2x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

∫(5x−2ex+2)dx=∫5xdx−2∫exdx+∫2dx=5xln⁡5−2ex+2x+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Sum of Exponential Functions
content.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({5}^{x}-2{e}^{x}+2)\,\text{d}x & =\int {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x-2\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int 2\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}}{ln⁡5}-2{e}^{x}+2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 15
?

∫(2⋅5x−ex+x3)dx=

a
5xln⁡5−e5x+x33+C
b
2⋅xln⁡5+ex+x33+C
c
5⋅5xln⁡5+ex+x32+C
d
2⋅5xln⁡|x|−2ex+x44+C
e
2⋅5xln⁡5−ex+x44+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrate term by term: 2·5^x gives 2·5^x/ln(5), −e^x gives −e^x, and x³ gives x⁴/4. Adding C yields option e.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2\cdot {5}^{x}-{e}^{x}+{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =2\int {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x-\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{5}^{x}}{ln⁡5}-{e}^{x}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

∫(2⋅5x−ex+x3)dx=2∫5xdx−∫exdx+∫x3dx=2⋅5xln⁡5−ex+x44+C.

content.knowledge_point: Integrating a Sum of Exponential Functions
content.worked_solution:
Here, we combine the sum rule and our exponential rules to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2\cdot {5}^{x}-{e}^{x}+{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =2\int {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x-\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x+\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{5}^{x}}{ln⁡5}-{e}^{x}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
